text: Number of test pieces One test piece for each component sheet of the window measuring 300 mm x 25 mm shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Flexibility test
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Flexibility test > Test method
text: The method used shall be that described in Annex 3, paragraph 12.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Flexibility test
text: Interpretation of results The vertical deviation of both component sheets shall be less than 50 mm after 60 seconds.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units
title: Headform test
text: Headform test

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test
text: Indices of difficulty of the secondary characteristics No secondary characteristic is involved.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test
text:
Number of test pieces Six flat test pieces (1,170 mm x 570 mm +0/-2 mm) or six complete parts shall be subjected to testing. The table below shows the type of samples subject to testing, in accordance with the dimensions of the glazing to be assessed.
|Type of window|Characteristic of window|Dimensions of flat sample|Alternative|
|---|---|---|---|
|Small window|Diameter D of the circle capable of being scribed: D < 150 mm and area of less than 200 cm^2|No test||
|Other than small window|Diameter D of the circle capable of being scribed: D < 400 mm and area of at least 200 cm^2|1,170 mm x 570 mm (material type testing and standard support frame)|Other part of same material, production procedure, thickness, colour with dimensions bigger than those of the original part, into which a 400 mm diameter circle can be scribed, and with a developed surface area of less than 1,170 mm x 570 mm (part type approval for the original part^1)|
||Diameter D of the circle capable of being scribed: 400 mm < D|1,170 mm x 570 mm (material type testing and standard support frame)|Real part (submitted for approval) (part type approval and dedicated support frame)|
_Note:_1 Original part dimensions are too small for performing the test.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test > Test method
text: The test method used shall be that described in Annex 3, paragraph 3.2.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test > Test method
text: For forward facing glazing situated forward of an occupant like partitions and separating windows which have impact probability (classification X/A) the drop height shall be 3 m. The HIC value shall also be measured.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test > Test method
text: For glazing like side windows, back windows and sunroofs which have reduced impact possibilities (classification X/B) the drop height shall be 1.5 m. The HIC value shall also be measured.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test > Test method
text: For glazing which do not have contact possibilities **,** as well as for small glazing and for all windows in trailer caravans there will be no headform testing.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test
text: Interpretation of results The test shall be deemed to have given a satisfactory result if the following conditions are fulfilled:

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test > Test method
text: The test piece is not penetrated nor shall it break into fully separate large pieces.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test > Test method
text: The HIC value is less than 1,000.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test > Test method
text: A set of test pieces submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the headform test if one of the following conditions is met:

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test > Test method
text: All the tests give satisfactory results, or

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Headform test > Test method
text: One test having given an unsatisfactory result, a further series of tests carried out on a new set of test pieces gives satisfactory results.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units
title: Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test
text: Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test
text: Indices of difficulty of the secondary characteristics: (1) Without obscuration(s) (2) With obscuration(s)

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test
text: Number of test pieces Ten flat square pieces of 300 mm +10/-0 mm side of the outer component sheet or ten substantially flat finished parts shall be subjected to testing. In this later case, the contact between the part and the supporting fixture shall be around the whole perimeter and of about 15 mm width. Upper and lower supporting frames shall be clamped together in a way that ensures that the movement of the test piece during the test shall not exceed 2 mm.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test > Test method
text: The method used shall be that prescribed in Annex 3, paragraph 2.1. Impact will be on the outer side of the test window

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test > Test method
text:
The height of drop for the various thickness values of the outer component of the window is given in the table below:
|Outer sheet thickness (mm)|Height of drop (m)|
|---|---|
|< 3|2|
|4|3|
|5|4|
|> 6|5|
For intermediate values of thickness in the interval between 3 mm and 6 mm the height of drop shall be interpolated.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: The ball test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the following conditions are met: (a) The ball does not penetrate the test piece (b) The test piece does not break into separate pieces. As a result of the impact, cracks and fissures in the test piece shall however be permitted.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: A set of test pieces submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the 227 g ball test if eight or more separate tests give a satisfactory result at the drop height. 5.5. 227 g ball test at -18 °C ± 2 °C

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: To minimize the temperature change of the test piece, the test shall be performed within 30 seconds of the removal of the test piece from the conditioning appliance.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: The test method shall be that described in paragraph 5.3. of this annex, except that the test temperature is -18 °C ± 2 °C.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Mechanical strength test 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results as in paragraph 5.4. of this annex.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units
title: Test resistance to the environment
text: Test resistance to the environment

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment
title: Test of resistance to abrasion
text: Test of resistance to abrasion

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 4., shall apply; the test is performed for either 1,000, 500 or 100 cycles to measure abrasion of the surface of the product.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion
text: Three flat square test pieces of 100 mm side for each type of surface shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion > Interpretation of results
text: In the case of glazing of class L, the abrasion test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the increase of haze after abrasion does not exceed 2 per cent after 1,000 cycles on the outer surface of the test sample and 4 per cent after 100 cycles on the inner surface of the test sample.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion > Interpretation of results
text: In the case of glazing of class M, the abrasion test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the increase of haze after abrasion does not exceed 10 per cent after 500 cycles on the outer surface of the test sample and 4 per cent after 100 cycles on the inner surface of the test sample.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion > Interpretation of results
text: In the case of glazing of Class L, for the abrasion on the outer surface of the test sample, either the abrasion test according to Annex 3, paragraph 4. or as an equivalent alternative the package of sand drop test, car-wash test and wiper test shall apply as described in Annex 17, paragraphs 6.1.2., 6.1.3. and 6.1.4.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion > Interpretation of results
text: For sun roofs, no abrasion test is required.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion
text: A set of samples for approval shall be considered satisfactory if all samples meet the requirements.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment
title: Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Test of resistance to simulated weathering

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 6.4. shall apply. The total ultraviolet radiant exposure with the long arc xenon lamp shall be 500 MJ/m2 . During irradiation the test pieces shall be exposed to water spray in continuous cycles. During a cycle of 120 minutes the test pieces are exposed to light without water spray for 102 minutes and to light with water spray for 18 minutes.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Other methods giving equivalent results shall be allowed.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Number of test pieces Three flat test pieces 130 mm x 40 mm cut from the outer skin of the window shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering > Interpretation of results
text: The resistance to the simulated weathering shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if:

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering > Interpretation of results
text: The light transmittance measured in accordance with Annex 3, paragraph 9.1 does not fall below 95 per cent of the pre-weathering value. Additionally, for windows which are required for driver visibility the value shall not fall below 70 per cent.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering > Interpretation of results
text: No bubbles or other visible decompositions, discolorations, milkiness or crazing shall occur during weathering.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: A set of test pieces submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the resistance to simulated weathering if all test pieces give satisfactory results.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment
title: Cross-cut test
text: Cross-cut test

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 13., shall apply only to coated products.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
text: The cross-cut test shall be carried out on one of the test pieces from paragraph 6.2.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test > Interpretation of results
text: The cross-cut test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if: The cross-cut value Gt1 is met.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test > Interpretation of results
text: The test piece shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of approval if the test gives satisfactory results.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment
title: Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Resistance-to-humidity test

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 7., shall apply.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Ten square pieces or test windows of 300 x 300 mm side or ten original parts shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: The humidity test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if:

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: No visible decompositions like bubbles or milkiness occur on any sample, 6.4.3.1.2. and if the light transmittance measured according to Annex 3, paragraph 9.1. does not fall to less than 95 per cent of the pre-test value and additionally to no less than 70 per cent for any window required for driver visibility.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: After testing the test pieces shall be stored for at least 48 hours at a temperature of 23° C ± 2 °C and a relative humidity of 50 ± 5 per cent, and then subjected to the 227 g ball drop test described under paragraph 5. of this annex.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units
text: Optical qualities The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 9.1., shall apply for products which are requisite for driver visibility.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Test resistance to the environment
text: Interpretation of results A set of four samples shall be considered as satisfactory if all samples give satisfactory results.

text: Fire resistance test

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Fire resistance test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 10., shall apply.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Fire resistance test
text: Interpretation of results The test needs to be performed separately on both surfaces of the double glazed unit. The fire-resistance test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the burning rate is less than 110 mm/min.

heading: Annex 16 Rigid plastic multiple glazed units > Fire resistance test
text: For the purpose of approval a set of samples will be considered satisfactory if all samples give satisfactory results.

Three samples out of four, among which the cross-cut sample mentioned above when applicable, shall give satisfactory results for each chemical.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: Definition of type Rigid plastic windscreens shall be deemed to belong to different types if they differ in at least one of the following principal or secondary characteristics.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The principal characteristics are as follows:

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: Trade names or marks.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The chemical designation of the material.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The classification of the material by the manufacturer.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The process of manufacture.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The shape and dimensions. Rigid plastic windscreens shall be deemed to belong to one group for the purposes of tests of mechanical properties and of resistance to the environment.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The nominal thickness. The thickness tolerance limit for extruded plastic products is ± 10 per cent of the nominal thickness. For plastic products produced by other techniques (e.g. cast acrylic sheet), the acceptable thickness tolerance is given by the equation (thickness tolerance limits (mm) = ±(0.4 + 0.1 e) where e is the nominal thickness in millimetres. Reference Standard is ISO 7823/1.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The colouring of the plastic product.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The nature of the surface coating.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The secondary characteristics are as follows:

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The incorporation or otherwise of conductors.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
text: The incorporation or otherwise of obscuration bands.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens
title: General
text: General

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > General
text: In the case of rigid plastic windscreens the tests shall be conducted either on flat test pieces rigorously representative of the finished product or on finished parts.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > General
text: The test pieces shall be freed from protecting masking and have to be cleaned carefully before the test.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > General
text: They shall be stored for 48 hours at a temperature of 23 °C ± 2 °C and a relative humidity of 50 per cent ± 5 per cent.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Flexibility test

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
text: The cross-cut test shall be carried out on one of the test pieces from paragraph 6.2.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test

text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test > Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Resistance-to-humidity test

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 7. shall apply.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Ten flat square test pieces of 300 mm side or ten test pieces of same size cut from windscreens, or ten original parts shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: The humidity test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if:

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: No visible decompositions like bubbles or milkiness occur on any sample, and

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: The light transmittance measured according to Annex 3, paragraph 9.1. shall not fall to less than 95 per cent of the pre-test value and additionally to no less than 70 per cent, on any sample.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: After testing the test pieces shall be stored for at least 48 hours at a temperature of 23 °C ± 2 °C and a relative humidity of 50 per cent ± 5 per cent, and then subjected to the 227 g ball drop test, under ambient temperature, described under paragraph 5.3. of this annex.

text: Fire resistance test

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Fire resistance test
text: Interpretation of results The fire-resistance test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the burning rate is less than 110 mm/min.

heading: Annex 17 Rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Fire resistance test
text: For the purpose of approval a set of samples will be considered satisfactory if all samples give a satisfactory result.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: Definition of type Laminated rigid plastic panes shall be deemed to belong to different types if they differ in at least one of the following principal or secondary characteristics.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The principal characteristics are as follows:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: Trade names or marks.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The chemical designation of the single sheet material.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The classification of the material by the manufacturer.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The process of manufacture.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The shape and dimensions.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The nominal thickness 'e' of the pane, a manufacturing tolerance of ± n • x mm being allowed ('n' being the number of layers of rigid plastic in the pane and x is the manufacturing tolerance of the single rigid plastic sheets in the pane, its value is depending on the process of manufacture and being given in Annex 14, paragraph 1.1.6.).

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The nominal thickness of the interlayer or interlayers.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The nature and type of the interlayer or interlayers, e.g. PVB or other plastics-material interlayer or interlayers.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: Any special treatment which one of the layers of plastic may have undergone.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The colouring of the plastic product.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The nature of the surface coating.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The secondary characteristics are as follows:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The colouring (total or partial) of the interlayer or interlayers (colourless or tinted).

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The incorporation or otherwise of opaque obscuration.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
text: The presence or absence of conductors or heating elements.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
title: General
text: General

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > General
text: In the case of rigid plastic panes the tests shall be conducted either on flat test pieces rigorously representative of the finished product or on finished parts. All optical measurements shall be carried out on real parts.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > General
text: The test pieces shall be freed from protecting masking and have to be cleaned carefully before the test.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > General
text: They shall be stored for 48 hours at a temperature of 23 °C ± 2 °C and a relative humidity of 50 per cent ± 5 per cent.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > General
text: To describe the breaking behaviour under dynamical stress, classes will be created depending on the application of the plastics. These classes are related to contact probabilities of the human head with the plastic glazing and they contain different requirements concerning the headform test.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
title: Flexibility test
text: Flexibility test

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Flexibility test
text: Indices of difficulty of the secondary characteristics No secondary characteristic is involved.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Flexibility test
text: Number of test pieces One flat test piece measuring 300 mm x 25 mm shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Flexibility test
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Flexibility test > Test method
text: The method used shall be that described in Annex 3, paragraph 12.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Flexibility test
text: Interpretation of results For a test piece or sample to be considered rigid the vertical deflection of the test piece shall be less than or equal to 50 mm after 60 seconds.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
title: Headform test
text: Headform test

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test
text: Indices of difficulty of the secondary characteristics No secondary characteristic is involved.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test
text:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test > Test method
text: The method used shall be that described in Annex 3, paragraph 3.2.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test > Test method
text: For forward facing panes situated forward to an occupant and which have impact probability (classification XIV/A) the drop height shall be 3 m. The HIC value shall also be measured.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test > Test method
text: For side windows, back windows with limited impact possibilities (classification XIV /B) and sunroofs the drop height shall be 1.5 m. The HIC value shall be measured.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test > Test method
text: For panes which are not likely to be impacted as well as for small windows in motor vehicles and for all windows in trailers (classification XIV/C) the headform shall not be performed. A small window is a window into which a 150 mm diameter circle cannot be scribed.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test
text: Interpretation of results The test shall be deemed to have given a satisfactory result if the following conditions are fulfilled:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test > Test method
text: The test piece or sample is not penetrated nor shall it break into fully separate large pieces.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test > Test method
text: The HIC value is less than 1,000.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Headform test > Test method
text: A set of test pieces submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the headform test if all the tests give satisfactory results.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
title: Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test
text: Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test
text: Indices of difficulty of the secondary characteristics: (a) Without conductors, obscuration(s) or heating elements, (b) With conductors, obscuration(s) or heating elements.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test
text: Number of test pieces Ten flat square pieces of 300 +10/-0 mm side or ten substantially flat finished parts shall be subjected to testing. In this later case the contact between the part and the supporting fixture shall be around the whole perimeter and of about 15 mm width. Upper and lower supporting frames shall be clamped together in a way that ensures that the movement of the test piece during the test shall not exceed 2 mm.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test > Test method
text: The method used shall be that prescribed in Annex 3, paragraph 2.1.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test > Test method
text: The height of drop shall be 6 m.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: The ball test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the following conditions are met: (a) The ball does not penetrate the test piece, (b) The test piece does not break into separate pieces. As a result of the impact, cracks and fissures in the test piece shall however be permitted.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: A set of test pieces submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the 227 g ball test if eight or more separate tests give a satisfactory result at the drop height.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: The ambient temperature ball drop test shall be only performed after the humidity test of paragraph 6.4.4. of this annex. 5.5. 227 g ball test at -18 °C ± 2 °C.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: To minimize the temperature change of the test piece, the test shall be performed within 30 seconds of the removal of the test piece from the conditioning appliance.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: The test method shall be that described in paragraph 5.3. of this annex, except that the test temperature is -18 °C ± 2 °C.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Mechanical strength test — 227 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results as in paragraph 5.4. of this annex.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes
title: Test of resistance to the environment
text: Test of resistance to the environment

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Test of resistance to abrasion
text: Test of resistance to abrasion

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 4. shall apply; the test is performed for either 1,000, 500 or 100 cycles to measure abrasion of the surface of the product.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion
text: Three flat square test pieces of 100 mm side for each type of surface shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion > Interpretation of results
text: In the case of glazing of class L, the Taber abrasion test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the increase of haze after abrasion does not exceed 2 per cent after 1,000 cycles on the outer surface of the test sample and 4 per cent after 100 cycles on the inner surface of the test sample.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion > Interpretation of results
text: In the case of glazing of class M, the Taber abrasion test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the increase of haze after abrasion does not exceed 10 per cent after 500 cycles on the outer surface of the test sample and 4 per cent after 100 cycles on the inner surface of the test sample.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion > Interpretation of results
text: In the case of glazing of Class L for the abrasion on the outer surface of the test sample, either the Taber test or as an equivalent alternative the package of Sand drop test, Car-wash test and Wiper test shall apply as described in Annex 17, paragraphs 6.1.2., 6.1.3. and 6.1.4.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion > Interpretation of results
text: For sun roofs no abrasion test is required.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to abrasion
text: A set of samples for approval shall be considered satisfactory if all samples meet the requirements

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Test of resistance to simulated weathering

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 6.4. shall apply. The total ultraviolet radiant exposure with the long arc xenon lamp shall be 500 MJ/m2 . During irradiation the test pieces shall be exposed to water spray in continuous cycles. During a cycle of 120 minutes the test pieces are exposed to light without water spray for 102 minutes and to light with water spray for 18 minutes.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Other methods giving equivalent results shall be allowed.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Number of test pieces Three flat test pieces 130 mm x 40 mm cut from a flat sheet sample shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering > Interpretation of results
text: The resistance to the simulated weathering shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering > Interpretation of results
text: The light transmittance measured in accordance with Annex 3, paragraph 9.1. does not fall below 95 per cent of the pre-weathering value. Additionally, for windows which are required for driver visibility the value shall not fall below 70 per cent.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering > Interpretation of results
text: No bubbles or other visible decompositions, discolouration, milkiness or crazing shall occur during weathering.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: A set of test pieces or samples submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the resistance to simulated weathering if all test pieces have given a satisfactory result.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Cross-cut test
text: Cross-cut test

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 13. shall apply only to coated rigid products.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
text: The cross-cut test shall be carried out on one of the test pieces from paragraph 6.2.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test > Interpretation of results
text: The cross-cut test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test > Interpretation of results
text: At least the cross-cut value Gtl is met.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test > Interpretation of results
text: The test piece shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of approval if the test has given satisfactory results.

text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 7. shall apply.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Ten flat square test pieces of 300 mm side, or ten original parts shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: The humidity test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: No visible decompositions like bubbles or milkiness occur on any sample, and

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: The light transmittance measured according to Annex 3, paragraph 9.1. shall not fall to less than 95 per cent of the pre-test value and additionally to no less than 70 per cent, on any sample, for any window required for driver visibility.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: After testing the test pieces shall be stored for at least 48 hours at a temperature of 23 °C ± 2 °C and a relative humidity of 50 per cent ± 5 per cent, and then subjected to the 227 g ball drop test described under paragraph 5.3. of this annex.

title: Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Test of resistance to high temperature

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 5. shall apply

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Three square test pieces of at least 300 mm x 300 mm which have been cut from three panes, one edge of which corresponds to the upper edge of the glazing shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: The test for resistance to high temperature shall be considered to give a positive result if bubbles or other defects are not formed more than 15 mm from an uncut edge or 25 mm from a cut edge of the test piece or sample or more than 10 mm away of any cracks which may occur during the test.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: A set of test pieces or samples submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the test for resistance to high temperature if all the tests give a satisfactory result;

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment
text: Resistance-to-radiation test This test has to be performed at the discretion of the laboratory conducting the tests.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 6. shall apply.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Three test pieces of 76 mm x 300 mm shall be cut from the upper part of the pane in such a way that the upper edge of the test piece coincides with the upper edge of the pane. These test pieces shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: The test for resistance to radiation shall be deemed to have given a positive result if the following conditions are fulfilled:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: The total light transmittance when measured pursuant to paragraphs 9.1.1. and 9.1.2. of this annex does not fall below 95 per cent of the original value before irradiation and in any event does not fall:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: Below 70 per cent in the case of glass panes other than windscreens which are required to comply with the specifications regarding the driver's field of view in all directions;

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: The test piece or sample may however show a slight coloration after irradiation when examined against a white background, but no other defect may be apparent.

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: A set of test pieces or samples submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the resistance-to-radiation test if one of the following conditions is fulfilled:

heading: Annex 18 Laminated rigid plastic panes > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: All the tests give a satisfactory result.

text: Optical qualities The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 9.1. shall apply for products which are requisite for driver visibility.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > General
text: In the case of laminated rigid plastic windscreens tests other than headform tests and tests of optical qualities shall be conducted on flat test pieces which are either cut from actual windscreens or are specially made for the purpose. In either case the test pieces shall be in all respects rigorously representative of the serially produced windscreens for which approval is sought.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > General
text: The test pieces shall be freed from protecting masking and have to be cleaned carefully before the test.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > General
text: They shall be stored for 48 hours at a temperature of 23 °C ± 2 °C and a relative humidity of 50 per cent ± 5 per cent.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens
title: Flexibility test
text: Flexibility test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Flexibility test
text: Indices of difficulty of the secondary characteristics No secondary characteristic is involved.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Flexibility test
text: Number of test pieces One flat test piece measuring 300 mm x 25 mm shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Flexibility test
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Flexibility test > Test method
text: The method used shall be that described in Annex 3, paragraph 12.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Flexibility test
text: Interpretation of results For a test piece or sample to be considered rigid the vertical deflection of the test piece shall be less than or equal to 50 mm after 60 seconds.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens
title: Headform test on a complete windscreen
text: Headform test on a complete windscreen

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Headform test on a complete windscreen
text: Indices of difficulty of the secondary characteristics No secondary characteristic is involved.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Headform test on a complete windscreen
text: Number of windscreens Six complete windscreens from the smallest-developed-area series and six complete windscreens from the largestdeveloped-area series selected in accordance with the provisions of Annex 13, shall be tested.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Headform test on a complete windscreen
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Headform test on a complete windscreen > Test method
text: The method used shall be that described in Annex 3, paragraph 3.2.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Headform test on a complete windscreen > Test method
text: The drop height shall be 3 m. The HIC value is also to be measured.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Headform test on a complete windscreen
text: Interpretation of results The test shall be deemed to have given a satisfactory result if the following conditions are fulfilled:

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Headform test on a complete windscreen > Test method
text: The sample is not penetrated nor shall it break into fully separate large pieces.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Headform test on a complete windscreen > Test method
text: The HIC value shall be less than 1,000.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Headform test on a complete windscreen > Test method
text: A set of samples submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the headform test if all the tests give satisfactory results,

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens
title: Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test
text: Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test
text: Indices of difficulty of the secondary characteristics: no secondary characteristics is involved

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test
text: Number of test pieces Twelve square test pieces of 300 +10/-0 mm shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test > Test method
text: The method used shall be that prescribed in Annex 3, paragraph 2.2.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test > Test method
text: The height of drop shall be 4 m at ambient temperature.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: The test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the ball does not pass through the glazing.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: A set of test pieces submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the 2,260 g ball test if eleven or more tests give a satisfactory result at the drop height. 5.2. 227 g ball test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test
text: Indices of difficulty of the secondary characteristics: (a) Without conductors, obscuration(s) or heating elements; (b) With conductors, obscuration(s) or heating elements.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test
text: Number of test pieces twenty square test pieces of 300 +10/-0 mm or ten substantially flat finished parts shall be subjected to testing. In this later case the contact between the part and the supporting fixture shall be around the whole perimeter and of about 15 mm width. Upper and lower supporting frames shall be clamped together in a way that ensures that the movement of the test piece during the test shall not exceed 2 mm.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test
title: Test method
text: Test method

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test > Test method
text: The method used shall be that prescribed in Annex 3, paragraph 2.1. Ten test pieces shall be tested at a temperature of +40 °C ± 2 °C and ten at a temperature of -18 °C ± 2 °C. To minimize the temperature change of the test piece, the test shall be performed within 30 seconds of the removal of the test piece from the conditioning appliance.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test > Test method
text: The height of drop shall be 9 m at +40 °C temperature and 8.5 m at -18 °C.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: The ball test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the following conditions are met: (a) The ball does not penetrate the test piece; (b) The test piece does not break into separate pieces. As a result of the impact, cracks and fissures in the test piece shall however be permitted.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Mechanical strength test 5.1. 2,260 g ball test > Interpretation of results
text: A set of test pieces submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the 227 g ball test if eight or more separate tests for each temperature give a satisfactory result at the drop height.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens
title: Test of resistance to the environment
text: Test of resistance to the environment

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
text: Test of resistance to abrasion For the purpose of testing the resistance to abrasion, either the Taber test or as an equivalent alternative the package of Sand drop test, Car-wash test and Wiper test shall be performed.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Taber test
text: Taber test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Taber test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 4. shall apply; the test is performed for 1,000 cycles to measure abrasion of the surface of the product.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Taber test
text: Three flat square test pieces of 100 mm for each type of surface shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Taber test
text: Interpretation of results The safety glazing shall be considered satisfactory with respect to abrasion resistance if the increase of haze as a result of abrasion of the test piece does not exceed 2 per cent.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Taber test
text: A set of samples for approval shall be considered satisfactory if all samples meet the requirements.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Sand Drop Test
text: Sand Drop Test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Sand Drop Test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 4.7. shall apply. Three kilograms of sand shall be used.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Sand Drop Test
text: Interpretation of results The safety glazing shall be considered satisfactory if the increase of haze of the test piece does not exceed 5 per cent.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Sand Drop Test
text: A set of samples for approval shall be considered satisfactory if all samples meet the requirements.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Car Wash Test
text: Car Wash Test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Car Wash Test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method A car wash equipment as described in paragraph 4.8.1. of Annex 3 to this Regulation shall be used. Ten washing operations (10 double passes) shall be carried out.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Car Wash Test
text: Three flat pieces 50 mm x 100 mm of each type shall be taken from the flattest part of the windscreen in the area specified in paragraph 2.2. of Annex 21 (test area A). The test shall be carried out on the face corresponding to the outside of the windscreen.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Car Wash Test
text: Interpretation of results The safety glazing shall be considered satisfactory if the increase of haze of the test piece does not exceed 2 per cent.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Car Wash Test
text: A set of samples for approval shall be considered satisfactory if all samples meet the requirements.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Wiper test
text: Wiper test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Wiper test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method A wiper laboratory equipment as described in paragraph 4.9.1. of Annex 3 to this Regulation shall be used. 20,000 wiper cycles shall be carried out.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Wiper test
text: Three absolutely flat test samples of 150 mm x 100 mm shall be tested. The test shall be carried out on the face corresponding to the outside of the windscreen.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Wiper test
text: Interpretation of results The safety glazing shall be considered satisfactory if the increase of haze as a result of abrasion of the test piece does not exceed 2 per cent.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Wiper test
text: A set of samples for approval shall be considered satisfactory if all samples meet the requirements.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Test of resistance to simulated weathering

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 6.4. shall apply. The total ultraviolet radiant exposure with the long arc xenon lamp shall be 500 MJ/m2 . During irradiation the test pieces shall be exposed to water spray in continuous cycles. During a cycle of 120 minutes the test pieces are exposed to light without water spray for 102 minutes, and to light with water spray for 18 minutes.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Other methods giving equivalent results shall be allowed.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: Number of test pieces Three flat test pieces 130 mm x 40 mm cut from a flat sheet sample shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering > Interpretation of results
text: The resistance to the simulated weathering shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if:

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering > Interpretation of results
text: The light transmittance measured in accordance with Annex 3, paragraph 9.1. does not fall below 95 per cent of the pre-weathering value. Additionally, the value shall not fall below 70 per cent.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering > Interpretation of results
text: No bubbles or other visible decompositions, discolourations, milkiness or crazing shall occur during weathering.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to simulated weathering
text: A set of test pieces or samples submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the resistance to simulated weathering if all test pieces have given a satisfactory result.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Cross-cut test
text: Cross-cut test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 13. shall apply only to coated rigid products.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
text: The cross-cut test shall be carried out on one of the test pieces from paragraph 6.2.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Cross-cut test > Interpretation of results
text: The cross-cut test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if at least the cross-cut value Gt1 is met.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Resistance-to-humidity test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 7. shall apply.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: Ten flat square test pieces of 300 mm side or ten test pieces of same size cut from windscreens, or ten original parts shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: The humidity test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if:

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: No visible decompositions like bubbles or milkiness occur on any sample, and

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test > Interpretation of results
text: The light transmittance measured according to Annex 3, paragraph 9.1. shall not fall to less than 95 per cent of the pre-test value and additionally to no less than 70 per cent, on any sample.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance-to-humidity test
text: After testing the test pieces shall be stored for at least 48 hours at a temperature of 23 °C ± 2 °C and a relative humidity of 50 per cent ± 5 per cent, and then subjected to the 227 g ball drop test, under ambient temperature and height of drop of 8.5 m, described under paragraph 5.2. of this annex.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Fire resistance test
text: Fire resistance test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Fire resistance test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 10. shall apply.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Fire resistance test
text: Interpretation of results The fire-resistance test shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the burning rate is less than 110 mm/min.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Fire resistance test
text: For the purpose of approval a set of samples will be considered satisfactory if all samples give a satisfactory result.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Resistance to chemicals
text: Resistance to chemicals

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance to chemicals
title: Immersion test
text: Immersion test

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance to chemicals > Immersion test
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 11.2.1. shall apply.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance to chemicals > Immersion test
text: Interpretation of results A set of four samples for each chemical shall be tested; for each chemical, one of these samples shall be cross-cut according to paragraph 13. of Annex 3. Three samples out of four, among which the cross-cut sample mentioned above, shall give satisfactory results for each chemical.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance to chemicals
title: Test under load
text: Test under load

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance to chemicals > Test under load
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 11.2.4. shall apply.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Resistance to chemicals > Test under load
text: Interpretation of results A set of four samples, not being the ones mentioned in paragraph 6.6.1. above, for each chemical shall be tested. Three samples out of four shall give satisfactory results for each chemical.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Test of resistance to high temperature

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 5. shall apply.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Three square test pieces of at least 300 mm x 300 mm which have been cut from three panes, one edge of which corresponds to the upper edge of the glazing shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: The test for resistance to high temperature shall be considered to give a positive result if bubbles or other defects are not formed more than 15 mm from an uncut edge or 25 mm from a cut edge of the test piece or sample or more than 10 mm away of any cracks which may occur during the test.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: A set of test pieces or samples submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the test for resistance to high temperature if all the tests give a satisfactory result.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
text: Resistance-to-radiation test This test has to be performed at the discretion of the laboratory conducting the tests.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 6. shall apply.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
text: Three test pieces of 76 mm x 300 mm shall be cut from the upper part of the pane in such a way that the upper edge of the test piece coincides with the upper edge of the pane. These test pieces shall be subjected to testing.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature
title: Interpretation of results
text: Interpretation of results

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: The test for resistance to radiation shall be deemed to have given a positive result if the following conditions are fulfilled:

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: The total light transmittance when measured pursuant to paragraphs 9.1.1. and 9.1.2. of this annex does not fall below 95 per cent of the original value before irradiation and in any event does not fall below 70 per cent.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: The test piece or sample may however show a slight coloration after irradiation when examined against a white background, but no other defect may be apparent.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: A set of test pieces or samples submitted for approval shall be considered satisfactory from the point of view of the resistance-to-radiation test if one of the following conditions is fulfilled:

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance to high temperature > Interpretation of results
text: All the tests give a satisfactory result.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
title: Test of resistance of temperature changes
text: Test of resistance of temperature changes

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance of temperature changes
text: Indices of difficulty and test method The requirements of Annex 3, paragraph 8. shall apply.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment > Test of resistance of temperature changes
text: Interpretation of results The test for resistance of temperature changes shall be considered to have given a satisfactory result if the test pieces do not show any evidence of cracking, clouding, separation of layers or other apparent deterioration.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens
text: Optical qualities The requirements concerning optical qualities set out in Annex 3, paragraph 9. shall apply to every type of windscreen.

heading: Annex 19 Laminated rigid plastic windscreens > Test of resistance to the environment
text: Interpretation of results A set of 4 samples shall be considered as satisfactory if all samples give satisfactory results.

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points
title: Test areas
text: Test areas

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: Two test areas shall be determined from the "V" points.

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: " _Test area A_ " is the area of the outer surface of the windscreen bounded by the intersection of the following four planes (see Figure 1a and 1b): (a) A plane inclined upwards from the X axis at 3°, passing through V1, and parallel to the Y axis (plane 1); (b) A plane inclined downwards from the X axis at 1°, passing through V2, and parallel to the Y axis (plane 2); (c) A vertical plane passing through V1 and V2 and inclined at 13° to the left of the X axis in the case of left-hand drive vehicles and to the right of the X axis in the case of right-hand drive vehicles (plane 3); (d) A vertical plane passing through V1 and V2 and inclined at 20° to the right of the X axis in the case of left-hand drive vehicles, to the left of the X axis in the case of right-hand drive vehicles (plane 4); (e) In case of a single central driving position, two planes upwards and downwards as defined in paragraphs 2.2. (a) and (b) above and two vertical plane passing through V1 and V2 and inclined at 15° to the left of the X axis (plane 3) and 15° to the right of the X axis (plane 4) (see Figure 1b).

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: " _Test area B_ " is the area of the outer surface of the windscreen bounded by the intersection of the following four planes: (a) A plane inclined upwards from the X axis at 7°, passing through V1, and parallel to the Y axis (plane 5); (b) A plane inclined downwards from the X axis at 5°, passing through V2, and parallel to the Y axis (plane 6); (c) A vertical plane passing through V1 and V2 and inclined at 17° to the left of the X axis in the case of left-hand drive vehicles and to the right of the X axis in the case of right-hand drive vehicles (plane 7); (d) A plane symmetrical with respect to plane 7 in relation to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle (plane 8).

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: The " _reduced test area B_ " is test area B with the exclusion of the following areas1 (see Figures 2 and 3). 1But taking into account the fact that the datum points as defined under paragraph 2.5. shall be located in the transparent area.

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: The test area A defined under paragraph 2.2., extended according to paragraph 9.2.2.1. of Annex 3;

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: At the discretion of the vehicle manufacturer, one of the two following paragraphs may apply:

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: Any opaque obscuration bounded downwards by plane 1 and laterally by plane 4 and its symmetrical in relation to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle (plane 4');

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: Any opaque obscuration bounded by the intersection of the outer surface of the windscreen: (a) With a plane inclined downwards from the X axis at 4°, passing through V2, and parallel to the Y axis (plane 9); (b) With plane 6; (c) With planes 7 and 8 or the edge of the outer surface of the windscreen if the intersection of plane 6 with plane 7 (plane 6 with plane 8) doesn't cross the outer surface of the windscreen;

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: An area within 25 mm from the edge of the outer surface of the windscreen or from any opaque obscuration. This area shall not impinge on the extended test area A.

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
text: Definition of the datum points (see Figure 3) The datum points are points situated at the intersection with the outer surface of the windscreen of lines radiating forward from the V points:

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas

heading: Annex 21 Procedure for determining test areas on windscreens of vehicles in relation to the "V" points > Test areas
